name: Treaty with the Piankeshaw, 1804 (Treaty of Vincennes)
aka: Treaty of August 27, 1804 with the Piankeshaw
nations: Piankeshaw (today represented by the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: The Piankeshaw ceded the land between the Ohio and Wabash rivers below Clark's grant and the Vincennes tract (Article 1).
The Piankeshaw acknowledged the Kaskaskia's right to sell the country the Kaskaskia had lately ceded (Article 2).
The United States would pay an additional annuity of $200 for ten years and delivered goods worth $700, which together were to be full compensation (Article 3).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission, having held that the Piankeshaw and the Delaware each had recognized title to an undivided half of Royce Area 49 when they ceded it in August 1804, awarded each of them $1,505,250, an amount the award describes as one-half the fair market value of Area 49, as additional compensation, with the $2,700 Piankeshaw treaty consideration later credited against it.

breaches.quote: being one-half the fair market value of certain lands (Royce Area 49)

landTaken: Royce Area 49, the tract between the Ohio and Wabash rivers in southernmost Indiana, ceded jointly by this treaty and the Delaware treaty of August 18, 1804 (Docket 289, 1968).
compensation: Treaty consideration credited at $2,700, with $1,255.65 of gratuitous offsets; final award entered February 24, 1971 on the parties' stipulation on offsets (Docket 289). The Piankeshaw figure in the final award could not be read cleanly from the scanned text.
today: The Commission recorded that Governor Harrison rejected the Miami and Potawatomi claims to Area 49 and treated the Delaware and Piankeshaw as its owners (Docket 289 findings, 1968).

plain.promised: An extra $200 a year for ten years and $700 in goods, as full payment for Piankeshaw land between the Ohio and Wabash rivers.
plain.happened: In 1970 the Indian Claims Commission awarded the Piankeshaw $1,505,250, their half share of the land's fair market value, as additional compensation, less the $2,700 treaty payment. The award does not use the word unconscionable.
plain.today: A final award was entered on February 24, 1971, but the Piankeshaw figure could not be read cleanly from the scanned text. Whether it was paid has not been traced.

nationVoice.nation: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says the Piankashaw made ten treaties with the United States beginning in 1795, that by this treaty they ceded their lands between the Wabash and the earlier Kaskaskia cession, after which most Piankashaw joined the Kaskaskia, Wea and Peoria near Ste. Genevieve before removal to Kansas and then Indian Territory, and that the red of its emblem stands for the trickery, tears and hardships its ancestors endured.

openQuestions: treaties.json names this entry for the 'Delaware, Miami, Piankishaw, Kaskaskia' with Royce cessions 48 and 49 and lists the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma as a present-day tribe. This instrument was made with the Piankeshaw alone; Area 48 was ceded by the Kaskaskia in 1803 (this treaty only acknowledged their right to sell it), and the Delaware ceded their half of Area 49 by a separate treaty of August 18, 1804. Not edited.

The December 11, 1970 opinion and findings in Docket 289 have no text in the OSU collection; the award is taken from the final award's recital, which does not use the word unconscionable. The basis is recorded as an award of additional compensation.
The Peoria Tribe's own account of the Piankeshaw cessions was not located in this pass.

Audit 2026-11-08: the final award (OSU id 1954) says each plaintiff was awarded '$1,505,250.00 being one-half the fair market value' of Area 49, so $1,505,250 is the Piankeshaw half share, not the whole value; 'what' and 'plain' reworded so they cannot be read as the whole. The Piankeshaw net figure in the final award is illegible in the scan and is still left out; the Delaware net, $1,497,246.11, is legible but belongs to the Delaware treaty of August 18, 1804.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 8): re-checked against kappler-78. The final award says each plaintiff, the Peoria Tribe for the Piankeshaw and the Delaware plaintiffs for the Delaware, was awarded $1,505,250.00, so the same figure is correctly carried on both files. The Piankeshaw net would be $1,501,294.35 by subtraction ($1,505,250 less $2,700 and $1,255.65); that is a computed figure, not read from the award, and is kept out of the record.
